sections.label: Infrastructure & Utilities
sections.summary: Transmission easement boundaries, overhead utility clearances, and underground utility coordination require critical documentation, graphical delineation, and formal coordination agreements across the site.

sections.label: Electrical Infrastructure
sections.summary: Austin Energy service approvals and electrical infrastructure coordination documentation are incomplete and must be obtained and documented on plans.

sections.label: Demolition & Construction Documentation
sections.summary: Demolition plan requires critical utility safety notes and documentation of utility removal procedures; construction staging requires defined vertical clearance zones.

sections.label: Plan Documentation & Administrative
sections.summary: Required addressing plan and administrative approvals must be documented and provided with the final plans.

comments.headline: Transmission easement boundaries and access requirements not graphically shown
comments.summary: Transmission easement location, ROW access corridor dimensions, and transmission structure positions are not depicted on site plan or construction plans, preventing verification of staging separation, access corridor maintenance, and utility pole placement compliance.
comments.crossDep: Transmission facility operator coordination for structure and easement location confirmation
comments.attn: Detail 3 flagged by single run; verify transmission facility locations with applicable utility operator before plan approval

details.text: 25-foot-wide transmission ROW access corridor with minimum 16-foot vertical clearance dimensions not graphically shown on site plan (Sheet 9) or erosion control plan (Sheet 5) to verify compliance with required corridor maintenance.

runComments.comment: Construction and staging plans do not demonstrate maintenance of a 25-foot-wide access corridor with minimum 16-foot vertical clearance along the full transmission ROW length. The transmission easement location is not clearly delineated on the Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan (Sheet 5), and no construction plan explicitly shows the transmission access corridor dimensions required by UCM 1.14.4.

Construction plans do not demonstrate maintenance of a 25-foot-wide access corridor with minimum 16-foot vertical clearance along the transmission ROW. Transmission easement boundaries and access corridor requirements are not graphically delineated on the site plan or erosion control plan.

Maintenance of 25-foot-wide transmission ROW access corridor with 16-foot minimum vertical clearance cannot be verified. Although Sheet 3 contains detailed transmission facility requirements, no transmission ROW or access corridor is graphically depicted or dimensioned on site plan (Sheet 9) or construction/staging plans to demonstrate the required 25-foot width and 16-foot vertical clearance for its full length.

details.text: Staging and temporary spoils areas' separation from transmission easement cannot be verified; easement boundaries not graphically delineated on construction or erosion control plans, despite Sheet 3 prohibiting materials storage within the easement.

runComments.comment: Cannot verify that staging and temporary spoils areas are not overlapping with transmission easement because the transmission easement boundary is not clearly delineated on the Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan. While Sheet 5 identifies a 'Staging and Storage Area' and 'Concrete Truck Cleanout' on the western side of the site, and Sheet 3 notes explicitly prohibit materials storage within the transmission easement, the transmission easement location is not graphically shown to verify compliance with the separation requirement.

Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes prohibit staging, spoils, and dumpsters within 25 feet of transmission structures. However, the transmission easement boundaries are not delineated on Sheet 5 (Erosion Control Plan) or Sheet 9 (Site Plan), making it impossible to verify that the shown staging area does not overlap transmission easement or violate 25-foot clearance from transmission structures.

Staging or temporary spoils areas overlapping utility line alignments or transmission easement cannot be verified. Although Sheet 3 specifies transmission easement restrictions (no spoils within 25 feet of transmission structures), a detailed staging/construction plan layout is not available in the reviewed sheets to confirm that staging areas avoid utility alignments and transmission easement encroachment.

details.text: Electric utility poles proposed within water easements or within 10 feet of large transmission structures cannot be verified because transmission structure locations are not depicted on any site plan sheet, despite 16 detailed transmission facility notes on Sheet 3.

runComments.comment: Electric utility poles proposed within water easements or within 10 feet of large electric transmission structures cannot be verified because transmission structures are not depicted on any site plan sheet or plat, despite Sheet 3 containing 16 detailed Electric Transmission Notes referencing transmission easements and structures. Applicability and compliance cannot be determined without clear identification of transmission facility location.

comments.headline: Overhead utility clearance zones lack graphical delineation and dimensioning
comments.summary: No distribution or transmission overhead conductor clearance envelopes, height limit lines, or clearance dimensions are shown on site plan or utility sheets, preventing verification of minimum sky-to-ground and radial separation requirements across varying site grades.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy for clearance envelope verification and site-specific analysis approval
comments.attn: Details 3–5 based on single-run findings; request AE-provided clearance envelope analysis and certified dimensions before final plan approval

details.text: No electrical clearance zones, transmission easement boundaries, or distribution conductor clearance envelopes are graphically delineated on any plan sheets (site plan, erosion control, electrical plan).

runComments.comment: No electrical clearance zones or envelopes are graphically delineated on any plan sheets. Transmission line safety buffers (including the 25-foot no-dig zone and transmission easement boundaries referenced in Sheet 3 General Notes) are not shown. Distribution overhead conductor clearance envelopes are not graphically represented.

Overhead electrical clearance zones are not graphically delineated on plans. Distribution clearance envelope boundaries (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial zone from outside conductor) are not shown on site plan or utility plan sheets. No transmission clearance envelope (which requires AE-provided site-specific analysis) is shown despite Sheet 3 referencing transmission facilities.

details.text: No horizontal dashed height limit lines depicted on site plan or erosion control plan to show transmission or distribution overhead conductor clearance envelope boundaries, despite Sheet 3 referencing transmission facilities.

runComments.comment: No horizontal dashed height limit lines are shown on the site plan or erosion control plan to delineate the overhead transmission conductor clearance envelope boundaries. Transmission structures and easement are referenced in Sheet 3 General Notes but are not graphically depicted with height limit annotations on site plan sheets.

Horizontal dashed height limit lines are not shown on plans to delineate AE overhead conductor clearance envelope boundaries. Site plan, grading plan, and utility plan sheets lack the required height limit line annotations that establish the vertical boundary of the overhead utility clearance zones.

details.text: Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from AE overhead primary, neutral, and secondary conductors along western and southern site boundaries cannot be verified; no clearance dimensions or measurement lines provided on electrical or site plans.

runComments.comment: Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from AE overhead primary, neutral, or secondary conductors cannot be verified. Overhead electric lines (OHE) are shown on the electrical plan and site plan along Valley View Road boundary, but no clearance dimension lines or measurements are provided from the outermost conductor to any customer facility edge, building, transformer pad, or other structure.

details.text: Minimum 15-foot radial clearance from AE overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors cannot be verified; no radial clearance envelopes or dimension arcs shown on utility plan (Sheet 21) or site plan (Sheet 9).

runComments.comment: Minimum 15-foot radial clearance from AE overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors cannot be verified. No radial clearance envelopes, dimension arcs, or measurements are shown on utility plan or site plan sheets from the outside conductor to any proposed customer facility.

details.text: Sloped or stepped dashed height limit lines not shown on grading plan (Sheet 11) or utility profile sheets to reflect grade-dependent conductor clearance boundaries; site elevation range 678.5' to 681'.

runComments.comment: Sloped or stepped dashed height limit lines are not shown on plans where overhead utilities are present on sites with non-uniform grade conditions. The site has sloped terrain (elevations ranging from ~678.5' to ~681' per benchmarks), but no profile-view height limit lines reflecting grade changes beneath overhead conductor spans are depicted on grading plan or utility profile sheets.

comments.headline: Recorded easements and transformer pad documentation missing
comments.summary: Two perpetual recorded easements encumbering approximately 19% of the property are not depicted on the site plan. Transformer pad locations lack AE easement encumbrances, required License Agreements, compliance with clearance requirements, and AE Design coordination.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy (transformer pad specifications and AE easement requirements); Public Works (easement verification and licensing requirements)
comments.attn: Coordinate with Austin Energy regarding final transformer pad locations and specifications before approval. Verify that proposed pad locations can satisfy minimum 10-foot clearance from all adjacent structures. Obtain copies of all recorded easement instruments from county records.

details.text: Two perpetual recorded easements encumber approximately 19% of the property but are not depicted on the site plan: Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres, NE interior, no-build zone) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres, NE corner).

runComments.comment: Two critical recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres; City of Austin Drainage Easement Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres) and four additional GIS-confirmed easements (10' Wastewater, 25' Drainage, 7.5' Public Utility, 10' Drainage) are not depicted on submitted site plan, preventing verification that utility easement boundaries do not encroach into proposed public right-of-way. Applicant must add all recorded easement boundaries to site plan before compliance can be verified.

Two perpetual recorded easements are not depicted on the submitted site plan: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres, NE interior, no-build zone, perpetual), and (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres, NE corner, perpetual). These recorded easements encumber approximately 19% of the property. All recorded easements must be depicted on the site plan, plat, and all relevant working drawings before approval. Current site plan compliance cannot be verified without these critical easements shown and building layout verified against them.

details.text: Transformer pad locations lack dedicated AE easement encumbrances and required License Agreements from AE Public Involvement. Pads 1 and 3 show only 'Vault Easement' (not AE easement); Pads 2 and 4 have no easement notation. Required License Agreements per UCM § 1.10.10.3 or City Manager licenses per § 14-11-41 are not documented.

runComments.comment: Two critical recorded easements required by law are not depicted on site plan: Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (2010070731, 0.31 acres, NE no-build zone) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (2011021137, 0.130 acres, NE corner). Additionally, transformer pads lack required AE easement documentation: Pads 1 & 3 show only 'Vault Easement' (not AE easement); Pads 2 & 4 have no easement notation. No dedicated AE easements visible encumbering transformer locations.

Submitted site plan does not show a dedicated AE easement encumbering transformer pad locations, nor is there notation of a License Agreement from AE Public Involvement per UCM § 1.10.10.3 or a City Manager license per § 14-11-41 for items within recorded utility easements. Utility easement status and licensing compliance cannot be verified from submitted documents. Provide AE easement plat or evidence of required license agreements.

The site plan identifies utility easements but does not include copies of required License Agreements or City Manager licenses. Items placed within private AE easements require a License Agreement from AE Public Involvement per UCM § 1.10.10.3. Items within public utility easements or public ROW require a City Manager license per § 14-11-41. Submit copies of all required licensing documentation for any structures, paving, or landscaping proposed within recorded easement boundaries before approval.

details.text: Transformer Pad 3 is positioned less than 5 feet from Unit 801 exterior wall and Pad 2 is less than 10 feet from Units 404 and 504, both violating UCM § 1.10.4 minimum 10-foot clearance from adjacent structures. All pads lack AE Design sizing specifications per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and coordination documentation with Austin Energy.

runComments.comment: Transformer Pad 3 is positioned less than 5 feet (nearly flush) against the exterior wall of Unit 801, violating the minimum 10-foot clearance requirement from any adjacent building or structure per UCM § 1.10.4(hot-stick/padlocked side). Transformer Pad 2, located in the tight corridor between Units 404 and 504, also appears to be positioned less than 10 feet from building exteriors. Additionally, no dedicated AE easement is shown on the site plan to encumber the transformer pad areas as required. Relocate transformer pads to satisfy minimum 10-foot clearance from all adjacent structures, and provide a dedicated AE easement plat encumbering the pad locations.

Transformer pads shown on the preliminary electrical design plan lack required specification and documentation. Pad dimensions must be sized per AE Design specifications (UCM § 1.5.2.6 requires customer to furnish pad per AE Design based on customer's AutoCAD site drawings). Each pad must be encumbered by a dedicated AE easement and protected by a License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3). Coordinate with Austin Energy to obtain final pad dimensions and establish recorded utility easements for each pad.

comments.headline: Austin Energy Service Approvals Not Documented
comments.summary: Multiple required Austin Energy approvals and coordination letters are absent from the submittal, preventing verification of electrical service readiness and design compliance.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy – service availability, design approval, and ESPA coordination
comments.attn: Clarify with Austin Energy whether ESPA submission and design approval are required before site plan approval (AE notes indicate some may follow regulatory exception). Verify Service Availability Letter requirement timing.

details.text: Electric Service Planning Application submission to Austin Energy and approval documentation not provided. ESPA is required before or concurrent with site plan approval.

runComments.comment: Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval is not documented in the plan set. While new Austin Energy electrical service is clearly proposed (transformers, meters, pull boxes, and underground lines shown on Sheet 21), the ESPA submission and approval status cannot be verified from the current submittal. ESPA is normally submitted after site plan approval per the regulatory exception; current status cannot be determined from available documents.

No Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval letter or submission documentation is visible in the site plan package. Austin Energy completeness check being marked complete does not constitute ESPA approval documentation.

Electric Service Planning Application submission to Austin Energy and approval documentation not provided in the site plan submittal package or supplementary documents. An ESPA is required before or concurrent with site plan approval for electrical service; verification of submission and approval status cannot be determined from available documents.

details.text: Austin Energy Utility clearance letter confirming service availability is not present in the submittal package.

runComments.comment: Austin Energy Utility (AEU) clearance or approval has not been located in the submittal package. No clearance letter from Austin Energy confirming service availability is present in the supplementary documents provided, though Austin Energy noted that the completeness check is complete.

Austin Energy Utility (AEU) clearance letter is not documented in the site plan package. While Austin Energy completeness check is noted as complete, no separate AEU clearance letter is visible to confirm approval.

details.text: Electric Service Availability Letter from Austin Energy Public Involvement has not been provided.

runComments.comment: Electric Service Availability Letter from Austin Energy Public Involvement has not been provided. Although the site is in Austin's established service territory, this letter may be required depending on AE's standard procedures for new service; its absence cannot be verified as compliant or deficient without clarification of AE service availability determination.

details.text: No evidence of Austin Energy approval for proposed transformer and pull box designs shown on Sheet 21.

runComments.comment: Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design with transformer and pull box locations, but no evidence of Austin Energy approval for these designs has been provided in the documents. Applicability cannot be determined without confirmation that final transformer and pull box designs are required before site plan approval.

comments.headline: Demolition plan missing critical utility safety notes
comments.summary: Sheet 8 demolition notes lack required transmission line safety requirements and general utility caution language, increasing risk to field personnel and utility infrastructure.

details.text: Missing transmission line safety clearances from demolition notes: 48-hour pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy, 10-foot barricade from transmission structures, warning signs, and prohibition on materials/spoils storage within transmission easement.

runComments.comment: Demolition plan sequence notes (Sheet 8, Block 9) do not address required safety clearances from transmission lines. Missing: (1) pre-construction safety meeting requirement ≥48 hours before commencement with Austin Energy; (2) barricade requirement 10 feet from all transmission structures, including guys and anchors; (3) warning signs under overhead transmission facilities; (4) prohibition on materials and spoils storage within the transmission easement. Current notes only reference Environmental Inspector meeting and utility abandonment.

Demolition plan (Sheet 8) Site Demolition Notes do not address required transmission line safety clearances detailed in Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes. Missing: (1) pre-construction safety meeting requirement with Austin Energy 48 hours before work commencement, (2) barricade requirement 10 feet from transmission structures, (3) warning signs under overhead transmission facilities, and (4) prohibition on materials or spoils storage within transmission easement.

Demolition plan notes do not address required safety clearances from transmission lines: pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy 48 hours before work commencement, barricades erected 10 feet from transmission structures, warning signs under overhead facilities, and prohibition on materials or spoils storage within transmission easement. Sheet 3 (General Notes) specifies transmission facility requirements but Sheet 8 demolition notes (Block 9, 10 items) do not reference or incorporate these safety requirements.

details.text: Missing contractor caution note requiring extreme care when working near at-grade utility appurtenances (meter boxes, cleanouts, valve boxes, pump stations, service pedestals, etc.).

runComments.comment: Demolition plan general notes do not include a requirement for contractor to use extreme caution when working near at-grade utility appurtenances. While the demolition notes address tree protection, utility abandonment, and safety meetings, there is no specific caution language warning the contractor about the electrical utility infrastructure present on the site.

Demolition plan general notes (Sheet 8, Block 9) do not include a note requiring contractor to exercise extreme caution when working near at-grade utility appurtenances (meter boxes, cleanouts, valve boxes, pump stations, service pedestals, etc.). This standard precaution is required on all demolition plans with proposed utility infrastructure.

comments.headline: Water utility tap crossing details incomplete and undimensioned
comments.summary: Sheet 20 water utility tap crossing under Valley View Road and existing water main lacks crossing method identification, clearance dimensions, and encasement specifications required to verify compliance with utility separation and roadway protection standards.
comments.applicableArea: Utilities & Infrastructure; Valley View Road Frontage
comments.crossDep: Austin Water for clearance and encasement specification verification; Austin Energy for underground facility coordination

details.text: AE underground facility clearance from water line at perpendicular crossings cannot be verified with required 12-inch minimum; Sheet 20 utility tap profile does not label horizontal or vertical clearance dimensions between water line and any AE underground electrical conduit.

runComments.comment: Water utility crossing shown on Sheet 20 crossing existing wastewater and gas lines, but no crossing detail identifies AE underground facility proximity or demonstrates 12-inch clearance. Verify that water line crossings do not impact AE underground conduit; if AE underground is present at these crossing locations, clearance dimensions must be labeled.

AE underground facility clearance from other utilities at perpendicular crossings cannot be verified with the required 12-inch minimum. Utility Tap Public Plan & Profile (Sheet 20) shows the proposed water line tap connection but does not label horizontal or vertical clearance dimensions between the water line and any AE underground electrical conduit at crossing points.

details.text: Water utility tap crossing method (trenchless vs. open-cut) not identified on Sheet 20 plan or profile; vertical separation distances not labeled; applicable standard (trenchless: 36" or 2× diameter per UCM 2.9.2.B.17 vs. open-cut: 12–18" per UCM 2.9.1.B.3) cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Sheet 20 profile shows water line (Wtr-Ln-A) crossing existing wastewater and gas lines, but the crossing method (trenchless vs. open-cut) is not identified on the plan or profile. Vertical separation distances are not labeled. Without crossing method designation and labeled clearance dimensions, the applicable separation standard cannot be verified.

Utility crossing method (trenchless vs. open-cut) cannot be clearly identified on plans, preventing verification of applicable separation standard. Sheet 20 utility tap profile does not explicitly state whether the proposed water line tap crossing under Valley View Road or existing water main is trenchless or open-cut, which determines whether UCM 2.9.2.B.17 (trenchless: 36 in or 2× diameter) or UCM 2.9.1.B.3 (open-cut: 12-18 in) applies.

details.text: Utility encasement specifications (piping material type, diameter, longitudinal extent) not provided on Sheet 20 Utility Tap Plan & Profile for water line crossing under Valley View Road per UCM 2.9.1.D.

runComments.comment: Sheet 20 profile shows water line crossing under Valley View Road (public roadway), but encasement specifications (material type, diameter, extent) are not provided on the crossing detail sheets. Confirm encasement piping specifications for utilities crossing under the roadway per UCM 2.9.1.D.

Encasement specifications are not provided for utilities crossing under roadways or structures. Utility Tap Plan & Profile (Sheet 20) does not reference or detail encasement material type, dimensions, or longitudinal extent specifications for the proposed utility tap crossing under Valley View Road.

comments.headline: Utility appurtenance clearances from poles and conductors undocumented
comments.summary: Clearance dimensions from customer service facilities, cleanouts, manhole, vault, and transformer locations to AE overhead poles, guy wires, and conductors are not dimensioned on any plan sheets, preventing verification of minimum separation requirements.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy for clearance review and written approval of appurtenance locations
comments.attn: All details based on single-run findings; request comprehensive clearance dimension review from Austin Energy for all customer facilities, appurtenances, and utility structures shown on plans

details.text: Fire demand meter vault vertical clearance from overhead line sag not labeled on Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 20); no Austin Energy clearance approval letter evident in project documentation.

runComments.comment: Vault vertical clearance from top of proposed structure to sag of lowest overhead power line is not labeled on plans. Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 20) indicates a fire demand meter vault connection but does not show or dimension its vertical proximity to the overhead electric line shown along Valley View Road. No Austin Energy written clearance approval letter is evident in the project file documentation reviewed.

details.text: Clearance dimension lines lack proper anchoring to outermost conductor (not utility pole centerline) on electrical design plan (Sheet 21) and site plan (Sheet 9).

runComments.comment: Clearance dimension lines cannot be verified as anchored to outermost conductor rather than utility pole centerline. No clearance dimensions are shown on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) or site plan (Sheet 9) to verify proper measurement reference points.

details.text: Customer service entrance facilities (transformer pads and electrical meters on Sheet 21) lack documented minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from AE poles and overhead lines other than service drop.

runComments.comment: Customer service entrance facilities and electrical appurtenances are not documented with minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from AE poles and overhead lines other than service drop. Sheet 21 shows transformer pad locations and electrical meter locations but provides no horizontal clearance dimension lines from these facilities to the OHE line or power poles shown along the property boundary.

details.text: Large-diameter wastewater cleanout horizontal clearance from AE utility poles and guy wires cannot be verified; Construction Details Sheet 26 shows specifications but no clearance dimensions provided.

runComments.comment: Large-diameter cleanout horizontal clearance from utility poles and guy wires cannot be verified. Construction Details Sheet 26 shows wastewater cleanout specifications but does not provide horizontal clearance dimensions from proposed cleanout locations to existing AE utility poles or guy wires on the site.

details.text: Storm drain manhole locations (Sheet 12) lack documented 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from AE power poles on western and southern property boundaries.

runComments.comment: Storm drain manhole horizontal clearance from Austin Energy overhead electric poles cannot be verified with the required 5-foot minimum. Storm Sewer Plan (Sheet 12) depicts multiple storm drain manholes across the site but does not provide horizontal clearance dimension lines from manhole locations to the AE power poles shown along the western and southern property boundaries.

comments.headline: Underground utility coordination agreements and ROW documentation missing
comments.summary: Plans do not identify joint-trench arrangements with Austin Energy, provide required joint-trench agreements, or document AULCC ROW assignment change approvals for utilities located within 24 inches of existing ROW facilities.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy for joint-trench coordination; Austin Utility Location Coordination Commission (AULCC) for ROW assignment change approval; Public Works for ROW authorization
comments.attn: Both details based on single-run findings; verify documentation status with AULCC and Austin Energy before plan approval

details.text: Underground infrastructure layout does not identify whether non-AE utilities (water, wastewater on Sheets 19) are proposed in joint trenches with AE underground conduit (Sheet 21), and no written joint-trench agreement with Austin Energy is evident.

runComments.comment: Underground electrical infrastructure shown on Sheet 21; water and wastewater utilities shown on Sheet 19. The plans do not clearly identify whether any non-AE utilities are proposed in joint trenches with AE underground conduit, or indicate if a written joint-trench agreement with Austin Energy is on file.

details.text: Utility tap located within 24 inches of existing ROW facility (Sheet 20) lacks documented AULCC Completeness Letter or formal ROW assignment change approval required by § 14-11-180(C).

runComments.comment: Proposed utility located within 24 inches of existing ROW facility cannot be verified with AULCC ROW assignment change approval documentation. Sheet 20 shows utility tap proximity to existing water main but does not reference AULCC Completeness Letter (ROW assignment change approval) or other formal AULCC authorization in the plan notes or project documentation reviewed.

comments.headline: Utility routing conflicts and incomplete documentation
comments.summary: Utility lines are routed through incompatible areas without complete documentation. Electrical and wastewater utilities cross the detention pond; water utility crosses a street tree planting zone; and new private utility routing to/from service connections is undefined.
comments.crossDep: Landscape/Arborist (street tree planting zone and root barriers); Watershed Management (detention pond design and utility conflicts); Public Works (ROW permitting and coordination)
comments.attn: Cannot fully verify routing details from submitted sheets — utility routing plans lack sufficient depth/profile detail. Confirm all electrical and wastewater utilities avoid the detention pond footprint entirely. Identify and protect root barrier zones for street trees. Clarify routing for new water and wastewater service connections to/from service points.

details.text: Electrical and wastewater utility lines are routed directly through the biofiltration/detention pond footprint, crossing through the sedimentation basin and biofiltration media on Sheet 15.

runComments.comment: Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan) shows electrical (E) and wastewater (WW) utility lines routed directly through the biofiltration/detention pond footprint, crossing through the sedimentation basin and biofiltration media. Utilities must not be routed under detention or retention ponds. Revise utility routing to avoid the pond area entirely.

details.text: Water utility line crosses through H.2 Street Yard planting zone along Valley View Road where street trees are present. No root barrier boundaries, designated planting zone delineations, or utility type designation (Austin Water vs. private service) are documented.

runComments.comment: Water utility line shown crossing through H.2 Street Yard planting zone along Valley View Road where street trees are present. However, no root barrier boundaries or designated planting zone delineations are marked on landscape plan, and utility type (Austin Water vs. private service) is not specified. Planting zone design cannot be verified from available documents.

details.text: New private water and wastewater service connections lack clear routing documentation. Site plan does not specify whether new utilities are routed through public ROW, private property, or dedicated easements.

runComments.comment: Existing public water and wastewater utilities in Valley View Road ROW are identified for demolition/removal. New private utility service connections are proposed. Site plan does not clearly show whether new private utilities are routed through public ROW or relocated to private property or dedicated easements. Final routing and ROW status cannot be determined from available plans.
